findingDetails.claim: the Product Owner format gate exercises a 145-line-smaller fork of the Sync Loop validator through a runner that cannot accept the shared runner's entry-script and blocking/advisory arguments

findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the Product Owner runner can be pointed at an external validator (the path is a literal), whether the files are identical (cmp reports they differ), and whether the local validator accepts a blocking/advisory argument (exits are only 64/66/1 and it is invoked with file arguments alone). Not re-read this iteration: vendor.json and SYNC.md, which could record a deliberate pin.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The Product Owner copy is a deliberately pinned, self-contained release artifact and the Sync Loop copy is the newer development variant, with the pin recorded elsewhere.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if vendor.json or SYNC.md records this validator as a pinned copy with an upstream commit or sha and a stated re-sync step.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both files read on disk; wc -l returned 1733 and 1878; cmp -s returned non-zero; both fixture runners' argument contracts read directly.
affectedSurfaceHints: AI Systems/z — Claude Project Sync Loop/validate-output-format.cjs
findingDetails.case: A deliverable breaks a rule that exists only in the Sync Loop copy; the Product Owner gate reports every format fixture passing and run_gates.sh exits 0, so the changelog records a clean format gate.

findingDetails.title: The release runner reports a clean pass while five checked-in parity and residency scripts never run
findingDetails.scopeProof: GATES array read in full (15 entries); benchmark/parity inventory taken on disk (5 .sh files, none referenced); header lines 29-37 read directly.
findingDetails.case: A release runs the documented single command, reads all 15 gates pass, and writes the changelog with receipt and residency parity unverified while no output line names the five scripts still owed.

findingDetails.title: Gate wiring derives the existence-check path from the second whitespace token, so any gate needing a flag before its script is reported MISSING
findingDetails.scopeProof: $2 extraction read at lines 63-65 and its consumer at 85-89; every current entry checked to begin with an interpreter then a path, so the defect is latent.
findingDetails.case: A maintainer adds a gate with an interpreter flag or inline environment assignment and sees MISSING beside a script they can confirm exists on disk.

spec_code.note: run_gates.sh stated exit contract (34-38) matches its implementation; the exception is finding 6, where the exit-0 summary does not name the parity exclusion the header declares.

checklist_evidence.note: vendor-sync.py:94-103 VENDOR_UPSTREAM_ROOT and upward .skilled walk match the guard at run_gates.sh:80; check_hub.py:701, example_lint.py:337, flow_check.py:636 and compose_board.py:1761 all implement --self-test, so none of those four gates is a silent no-op.
